title: Lords Command stack manifest (stack.toml)
description: One per stack root. Targets, memory stores, local repo paths and the fleet config may appear only in a private stack (checked).

topics.description: the controlled list of topics entries may tag; a public entry may use only the public stack's topics

roles.description: the controlled list of roles entries and targets may name; a public entry may use only the public stack's

checkouts.description: private only: local checkouts; sync writes each one's untracked agent files

worktrees.description: also every worktree of each checkout (git worktree list)

worktree_roots.description: only worktrees under these dirs get files; the rest are skipped and listed

adapters.description: adapter ids that get this repo's files (default: all)

skills.description: skill dirs tracked in the repo (paths in a checkout): indexed in place, never linked or moved

default_role.description: the role of a session here that no brief names one for: its entries go inline in the place's files

workspaces.description: private only: working dirs that are no git repo; they get the same untracked files as a checkout

targets.description: private only: user-level instruction files and skill dirs

name.description: unique among the targets: the ledger names a target by it (`target:<name>`), and the stack refuses two of one name

adapter.description: the adapter that writes this target, e.g. claude, codex

roles.description: the role whoever reads this file has; absent: unknown, so only every-role entries and a pointer to the rest

own_text.description: instructions: keep the text outside the managed block, or replace the whole file with it

via.description: instructions: the shared file that holds the composed text; this file gets only an include line

exclude.description: settings: instruction files the harness must skip

guards.description: settings: guards registered as the harness's hooks: rm (PreToolUse on Bash and PowerShell: an unguarded variable rm path, a git call skipping its hooks, git's help on a topic), queue (Stop), session (SessionStart), turn (UserPromptSubmit), child (SubagentStart: a native child's start file, `child_role`), role (UserPromptSubmit: the start of the role a session's launch names, `.lords/start-<role>.md`), time (PreToolUse on editor writes to Markdown and text files and on T3 messages: refuses a placeholder clock time, reminds of a future one). Claude Code runs all; Codex (`~/.codex/hooks.json`) runs rm, child, role and time

memory_stores.description: private only: agent memory dirs imported into memory/<name>/

audience.description: who may read its notes (default all)

native.description: adapters whose harness loads this store by itself

live.description: agents write this store's MEMORY.md: memory indexes name that file instead of listing the imported copies

fleet_config.description: private only: a fleet.toml whose host names count as private

place_files.description: per adapter id: how its place files are composed and measured

default_role_lines.description: whether the place's default role's lines for only some roles show in this adapter's place files, labelled, or stay in the role file

warn_bytes.description: the warning line for this adapter's place files in `check`, in bytes, in place of 75 % of its limit; the limit itself stays a refusal

child_role.description: the role a native subagent (one a session starts itself) starts as: each place's `.lords/child.md` carries that role's lines its place's file doesn't, which the `child` guard gives it

require_core.description: `check` refuses an entry of this stack that has neither a core line nor `start: detail` (intent, memory and in-repo skills need none)
